# Now THAT'S a Big Dragon! — mod

> An unofficial, open-source mod for the Steam idle game *Now THAT'S a Big Dragon!*. It
> translates the game into {{ site.data.languages | size }} languages, adds an in-game
> cheat widget, and plays the game unattended. It is injected over the Chrome DevTools
> Protocol and **modifies no game files** — closing the launcher removes it entirely.

This file exists because the facts below are worth quoting accurately. Every number in
it is generated from the repository, so it is either right or the build is broken.

## What it is

- **Name:** Now THAT'S a Big Dragon! — mod. Repository: <https://github.com/myso-kr/now-thats-a-big-dragon-mod>
- **Licence:** MIT for the code. The translations are derivative works of the game's text and carry no licence grant.
- **Platform:** Windows. The launcher is a single Rust binary with no runtime dependency — Node.js is not required to use it.
- **Method:** the launcher starts the game with `--remote-debugging-port=9223` and rewrites responses in memory over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. No file on disk is changed, and Steam's file integrity check passes.
- **Not affiliated** with the game's developer or publisher, or with Valve.

## By the numbers

- **{{ site.data.languages | size }} languages** ship today, covering **51.10% of Steam users** by language share.
- Each translation is **620 UI strings and 32 dialogue scripts**.
- **123 characters** were drawn into the game's own font `Everyday_Standard` so that translated text sits on the same 6 px/em grid as the rest of the interface; 56 more into `High_Birth` and 7 into Galmuri9.
- Greek needed the most work: no bundled pixel font draws Greek at 6 px/em, so all **67 letters of the monotonic alphabet** were drawn onto the game's own grid rather than borrowed a size too large.
- **451 JavaScript tests and 142 Rust tests** run on every push, plus byte-for-byte comparison of the Node and Rust implementations against a real game bundle.

## The three things it does

1. **Language patch.** Languages are *added* to the game's own settings screen — flag, name and time units included. The five the game already ships (English, French, German, Portuguese, Turkish) are left alone, so the choice stays the player's.
2. **Cheat widget (F8).** Resources, upgrades and game speed. Steam achievement and stat submission is blocked by default.
3. **Autoplay (F9).** Buys units and upgrades, fights, answers dialogue, crawls dungeons and repeats chapters, unattended.

## Warnings worth repeating

- A save can be corrupted by cheats or autoplay. Back it up before the first run.
- Turning off the achievement block and then cheating writes unearned achievements to the Steam account permanently.
- `--remote-debugging-port=9223` has no authentication. Any program on the same machine can attach to the game while the mod is running.
